# Settings

Every setting the engine, its plugins and the editor declare, by category:
`physics/solver_iterations` is `[physics] solver_iterations` in `project.toml`.
A project setting ships with the game; an editor setting is the person's, kept
in their `editor.toml`. A host setting describes the running process, its window,
its checker and its own files, so the editor keeps its own when it opens a game
to edit. Read this before declaring a setting: one that answers the same
question as an old one is a second way to say it.

## android

<table>
<thead><tr><th>key</th><th>type</th><th>default</th><th>notes</th><th>what it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>application_id</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>The identifier Play resolves an OAuth client, a licence and an update against. Required to export.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>display_name</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>The name under the icon. Empty means [application] name.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>version</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>versionName: what a player is shown. Required to export.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>version_code</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>0</code></td><td></td><td>versionCode: what Play orders updates by, and the only one it reads. Required to export; 0 is unset.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>min_sdk</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>0</code></td><td></td><td>The API floor. 0 defers to the template&#x27;s own, which is what its libraries were built against.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>target_sdk</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>36</code></td><td></td><td>The API this game says it was written for. Google Play takes a new app or an update only at 36 or later.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>abis</code></td><td>flags</td><td><code>[]</code></td><td></td><td>Which of the template&#x27;s ABIs the export keeps. None named means every one it carries, so a game that says nothing ships everywhere.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>keystore</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>A project-relative keystore. Without one an export needs --sign debug, which installs on a device and ships nowhere.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>key</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>Which key in that keystore signs.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>bundletool</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>Where bundletool.jar is. Empty looks at BALAUR_ANDROID_BUNDLETOOL and then beside the SDK; Google ships it on its own, not in the SDK.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## export

<table>
<thead><tr><th>key</th><th>type</th><th>default</th><th>notes</th><th>what it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>runtime</code></td><td>enum</td><td><code>&quot;auto&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>The runtime a game is put on. 2d and 3d carry one physics world each and weigh less, and auto takes the smallest the scenes and scripts fit, or the full one where only that is on hand; name one where a script builds a component&#x27;s name at run time. A server target keeps its own. Per target through that target&#x27;s override.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>output</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>A project-relative directory; each target gets a subdirectory of it. Empty exports where the command stands.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>strip</code></td><td>bool</td><td><code>false</code></td><td></td><td>Drop an asset no scene, script or include glob names. Off by default: a script may compute a path this cannot see, and losing an asset is worse than shipping one.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>include</code></td><td>list of string</td><td><code>[]</code></td><td></td><td>Globs an export includes whatever else it decides, for the paths a script builds at run time.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>image_recode</code></td><td>enum</td><td><code>&quot;webp&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>How an image is re-encoded on the way into the pack, kept only where it comes out smaller. Every mode keeps the size; quantized is the one that does not keep the pixels.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>image_quality</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>80</code></td><td></td><td>imagequant&#x27;s quality target, which image_recode = &quot;quantized&quot; reads and every other mode ignores.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>font_recode</code></td><td>enum</td><td><code>&quot;original&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>Whether a font is cut down to the characters the project&#x27;s scenes and scripts name.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>font_ranges</code></td><td>list of string</td><td><code>[]</code></td><td></td><td>Code points a subset font keeps beyond the ones found in the project, as first-last hex ranges (&quot;0020-00FF&quot;), for text from a server or typed by a player.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>font_original</code></td><td>list of string</td><td><code>[]</code></td><td></td><td>Faces that ship whole however font_recode is set, as globs: the one a text field draws with cannot be subset to the characters this project happens to contain.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>audio_recode</code></td><td>enum</td><td><code>&quot;flac&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>How uncompressed audio is re-encoded, kept only where it comes out smaller. flac keeps every sample; vorbis does not.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>audio_quality</code></td><td>float</td><td><code>0.5</code></td><td></td><td>libvorbis&#x27;s quality, which audio_recode = &quot;vorbis&quot; reads and every other mode ignores.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>tags</code></td><td>list of string</td><td><code>[]</code></td><td></td><td>Names this build answers to besides its platform&#x27;s, such as demo or store. An override or an asset variant may be written for any of them; per target, set it under that target&#x27;s override.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>max_size</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>0</code></td><td></td><td>The longest side an image ships at, in pixels; 0 keeps every size. Set it per target to ship a phone a smaller art set. Pixel art and bitmap font pages are never capped, and a sprite keeps the size it was drawn at.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>native_scripts</code></td><td>enum</td><td><code>&quot;auto&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>Ship the scripts as native code, built from their C with Xcode for an Apple target or clang and lld for any. auto falls back to the target&#x27;s engine when no compiler is found, on fails the export instead, off never builds it. Per target through that target&#x27;s override.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<tr><td><code>jitter_ticks</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>3</code></td><td>editor</td><td>Extra ticks drawn per payload. Jitter is what reorders a stream.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>loss</code></td><td>float</td><td><code>0.05</code></td><td>editor</td><td>The fraction of datagrams dropped. Datagrams only: losing a reliable payload would break the transport&#x27;s contract.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>transport</code></td><td>enum</td><td><code>&quot;webtransport&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>What a host listens with: QUIC datagrams, or a websocket where UDP is blocked.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>address</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;127.0.0.1:0&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>Where a host listens. 0.0.0.0 lets other machines in; port 0 takes any free one.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>players</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>2</code></td><td></td><td>How many slots fill before a match starts on its own; 0 waits for the host&#x27;s <code>start</code>.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scene</code></td><td>string</td><td><code>&quot;&quot;</code></td><td></td><td>The scene a match loads on every machine; empty for the main scene.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>depth</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>16</code></td><td></td><td>Snapshots kept for rollback: how many ticks late an input can still be answered.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>timeout_seconds</code></td><td>float</td><td><code>5.0</code></td><td></td><td>Seconds a join may take, and a link may go silent, before it is dropped.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<tr><td><code>soft_recovery/self_stand_down</code></td><td>bool</td><td><code>true</code></td><td></td><td>Let go of a tangled part&#x27;s own contacts, so its elasticity undoes the tangle.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>soft_resweep_strain</code></td><td>float</td><td><code>0.75</code></td><td></td><td>The strain past which a soft body&#x27;s constraint is solved again after the contacts in every substep, so a light body under heavier ones is not torn.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>solver_iterations</code></td><td>float</td><td><code>4.0</code></td><td></td><td>Solver iterations per step. More is stabler and slower; every value here changes results, so a recording only replays against the same numbers.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>static_contact_frequency_hz</code></td><td>float</td><td><code>60.0</code></td><td></td><td>The same, for a contact with a body that never moves.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>threads</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>0</code></td><td>on restart</td><td>How many threads the solver may take. 0 is the performance cores where the machine has two kinds of core, else every core.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>transmission_steps</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>1</code></td><td></td><td>How many layers of glass seen through glass are drawn; each costs another snapshot of the scene and another glass pass.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>probe_capture_size_pixels</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>256</code></td><td></td><td>Side of each cube face a <code>reflection_probe</code> captures, and the width of every probe map, which all probes share. A change clears every map and captures the probes again.</td></tr>

</table>

<tr><td><code>vsync</code></td><td>bool</td><td><code>true</code></td><td>host</td><td>Present in step with the display.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>msaa</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>1</code></td><td>host</td><td>Samples per pixel. 1 is off and 4 is the only other count the renderer offers; it costs two render targets of four samples each.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>max_fps</code></td><td>int</td><td><code>0</code></td><td>host, on restart</td><td>The most frames a second the loop draws. Zero paces it against the tick instead, which is what vsync already does on a display that runs at the tick rate.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>low_processor</code></td><td>bool</td><td><code>false</code></td><td>host, on restart</td><td>Run a frame only when something asks for one: input, ui.request_repaint, a log line, a changed file or work finished on another thread. What a tool that sits still wants; a game that moves every frame leaves it off.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
